coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Hoedown Yard 3 (HDY3)
record.summary: The northern parcel of the PG&E-owned Hoedown Yard at Illinois and 22nd Streets, zoned residential under the Pier 70 SUD and D4D (65 ft) but not part of Brookfield's 28-Acre Project: the City holds an option to buy the roughly 3-acre yard from PG&E, subdivide it into three parcels and offer them for sale, with an Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District over the yard meant to fund Pier 70's affordable housing. No sale, developer or construction has been recorded.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- 'planned' here reflects only that the adopted D4D designates this block; no source read reports a project, a developer or a start date for it. The land is still owned by PG&E: Port Item 9B (Sept 22, 2017, Table 3) says 'The City has an option to purchase the approximately 3-acre Hoedown Yard from PG&E', and Port Item 11A (Aug 7, 2026) lists 'approximately 3 acres owned by PG&E known as the Hoedown Yard' in the Pier 70 Special Use District; none of the sources read says that option has been exercised. It is part of the Hoedown Yard, which the D4D (Section 1) describes as owned by Pacific Gas and Electric (PG&E), with a City option to acquire it, and which is outside Brookfield's 28-Acre Site. The D4D gives the yard's Assessor lots as Block 4120 Lot 002 and Block 4110 Lot 008A (Port Item 9B gives 4120/002 and 4711/008A); DataSF's Assessor layer lists 4120002 and 4110008A (1021 Illinois St) as active lots, and this hand-traced block overlaps them, but the overlay of approximate geometry is not an identification of this block's own lot. RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. SNAPPED 2026-09-17: this block's north edge had drifted 1.26m south of PKS's own south edge (both blocks were independently re-measured at different times and no longer shared an exact boundary, despite the diagram showing them as one continuous fill with only an internal divider line). Snapped this block's NW/NE corners to PKS's south-edge coordinates exactly, closing the gap to 0m. RE-SNAPPED 2026-09-17 (same day): PKS itself was found to be badly mispositioned (60% of its area was being clipped away against the real 21st St -- see the Parcel K South (PKS) record) and was shifted ~25m south to ground-truth against the real street. Re-snapped this block's NW/NE corners to PKS's new south edge to stay attached; area dropped from ~2,699 to ~1,508 sq m as a direct, expected consequence of PKS moving into what was previously this block's own north portion. This block's own south/diagonal portion (touching HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground) is unchanged. INVESTIGATED 2026-09-17 (after this block was noted to look too small relative to its peers in the drawing): checked whether this shrinkage is a real bug (i.e., whether the same northward transform bias found on PKS/C1/PKN/Building 113-116 also affects this block's own south/diagonal portion, which would justify shifting HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground south too, restoring this block's diagram-implied size while keeping everything attached). Tested this directly: interpolated the real, official 22nd St centerline's latitude at HDY1/2's own south-edge longitudes (the nearest independently-checkable real street to this cluster) and compared to HDY1/2's current south edge -- found a clean ~14m gap with NO overlap, unlike PKS's 60% real-street overlap that justified its own correction. This is the opposite signature from a 'drawn too far north' bug: if the same bias reached this far south, HDY1/2 would itself be overlapping 22nd St, not comfortably clear of it. Conclusion: the 21st-St-row bias is local to that row and does not extend to this block's own south portion or to HDY1/2/Irish Hill Playground -- there is no evidence basis to shift them south to recover this block's pre-fix size. This block's current, smaller size is treated as the accurate, forced consequence of ground-truthing PKS (which shares this block's own north edge), not an unresolved bug. This conclusion is stated explicitly because Pier & Point does not fabricate geometry: if a future source shows this block's own south/diagonal corners were independently misread (a diagram-reading error, not a bias-correction consequence), that would still warrant revisiting this specific block on its own. DataSF's active lots 4110008A (6,101 m2) and 4120002 (5,997 m2) are the Hoedown Yard lots (the D4D and Port Item 9B give the yard as Block 4120 Lot 002 and Block 4110 Lot 008A, and the Port memo expects it to be subdivided into three parcels). Lot 4110008A overlaps this drawing by 2,344 m2 and lot 4120002 by 0 m2; each also lies under other drawn blocks and the Irish Hill Playground, so neither is this block's own lot, and the drawing is kept until the yard is subdivided.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The Hoedown Yard is PG&E's own Assessor land, not part of Brookfield's 28-acre site: the D4D (Section 1) gives it as Assessor's Block 4120/Lot 002 and Block 4110/Lot 008A (Port Item 9B: 4120/002 and 4711/008A), owned by PG&E with a City option to acquire it, and the Port memo says it will be subdivided into three separate parcels. The earlier statement that it is part of Brookfield's site and not subdivided is withdrawn; this record uses hand-traced approximate geometry because the yard has not been subdivided into the D4D's HDY parcels.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential in all three D4D land-use scenarios (Figures 1.5.5-1.5.7; not 'parking support' as sometimes described secondhand), 65 ft max per Figure 6.4.2 (a uniform height, not a 40-65 ft range). Part of the approximately 3.6-acre 'Hoedown Yard' (HDY) at Illinois and 22nd streets, which the D4D describes as currently owned by PG&E; the parcel takes its name from the yard. Shown as a separate parcel from HDY1/2 in the D4D's own figure. No construction-start source found.

open_questions: Whether the City has exercised its option to buy the Hoedown Yard from PG&E: no source read says. The Port's August 2026 Item 11A (p.2) still describes the yard as 'approximately 3 acres owned by PG&E'. The financing district itself was formed in 2018 (see the milestones).

The Port's 2026 proposed phasing plan (Item 11A, Exhibit A, p.8) shows the Hoedown Yard parcels (HDY1/2 and HDY3) outside every phase outline, since they are not part of the 28-Acre Project, so no phase is recorded here. Parcel K South, by contrast, sits inside the Phase 2B outline.
Assessor block/lot for the yard is given as 4120/002 and 4711/008A in the 2017 memo but 4120/002 and 4110/008A in the D4D; one is a typo, unresolved.

No basis for an expected-completion date was found: the Port's Aug 3, 2017 staff report (Item 11A, p.21, DDA major terms) says 'Parcel K North and the Hoedown Yard, while in the SUD, are not part of the Project', so the Hoedown Yard is a separate transaction from the 28-Acre Project; the Port's 2026 proposed phasing plan shows it outside every phase outline; no source read gives a schedule for the City's PG&E purchase option, so this record stays undated rather than borrow the 28-Acre Project's buildout target.

Ownership and area of the Hoedown Yard: the D4D gives an approximately 3.6-acre parcel and the DDA terms 'approximately 3-acre', including a 0.2-acre unbuilt Michigan Street right-of-way easement. The D4D describes the yard as currently owned by PG&E, with a City option to acquire it if PG&E can find a new location for its heavy industrial use.
